content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], I am trying to extend my inputs up to I48 and outputs up to Q19. What is the method for extension? This would help with clearer labeling for programming. Please see the attachment.
This is not feasible because one [product_name] [article_no] supports only 24 digital inputs (DI) and 20 digital outputs (DO).
Hello [user_name], To achieve that, you would need a second module connected via the network. This would give you in total 48 inputs, 40 outputs, and 800 function blocks.

That doesn't address the main question! Expanding the label list for inputs and outputs is unrelated to hardware limits. The list in [product_name] programming software is preset to 24 inputs and 20 outputs for each module.
Exactly! You can't create documentation for something that doesn't exist. Adding a second module means a separate program and documentation for each.
You're missing the point. The original poster wants the ability to extend I/O name lists in the programming software, so instead of just I1-I24 and Q1-Q20, you'd have I1-I48 and Q1-Q40.
I'm aware, but what's the purpose? The module can't handle more than its limits, so the list matches the actual hardware.
But then, why suggest using a second module? Each module still only has I1 to I24 and Q1 to Q20.
Then please explain how you would connect I40 or Q32 to a single module...
As mentioned before, your suggestion doesn't make sense.

analysis.insight_summary: The core discussion revolves around a user's wish to increase the input and output label range within the [product_name] programming environment, primarily for improved organization. Other contributors clarify that hardware constraints mean only a certain number of inputs and outputs can be managed, and the software reflects these limits—making label extension impractical. There are misunderstandings in the thread about whether more labels can be added or more hardware connected, but ultimately, the system has fixed limits that cannot be bypassed through software labeling alone.
analysis.user_expectations: The user would like to expand the labeling range for inputs and outputs in the [product_name] programming system beyond device limits to help with program organization and clarity.
